newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt higher at late afternoon.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt higher at late afternoon.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were higher late Tuesday as Brady bonds generally outperformed the U.S. Treasury securities market, sources said.

"We generally outperformed Treasuries," said one emerging market debt trader at a major U.S. investment firm. However, the source believes this year's spectacular rally in the emerging debt markets may be a little bit overdone and could experience some year-end selling.
Nonetheless, Nigerian par bonds were 2-5/8 stronger at 68-1/8 bid and UMS-26 bonds were 1-1/8 higher at 106-1/8 bid.
Another market source attributed Tuesday's gains in the Brady market to some new cash coming into the market.

"I think there is probably some new money coming into the market right now and I expect that to continue in 1997," he said, adding expectations of more declines in interest rates caused par bonds to outperform floating rate instruments.

Indeed, Argentine pars bonds were 1-3/4 firmer at 65-1/8 bid, while FRB's were 3/8 better at 87 bid. Elsewhere, Venezuelan pars bonds were 1/2 stronger at 77-1/4 bid and its FLIRBs were 3/8 firmer at 88-1/4 bid.
